decisions.reason: After two years without any visible negative signal, this core rye bread appears to meet aspiration levels and uses existing recipes, production routines, and channels efficiently.
As a flagship seasonal product with external gold-medal recognition, the premium raisin stollen is clearly above aspiration and highly unlikely to be withdrawn.
This seeded rye mixed bread fits the established assortment closely, and continued market presence suggests results are at least acceptable relative to comparable breads.
The dark barley malt rye bread remains somewhat niche and overlapping with other rye products, but absent clear underperformance a bakery with some slack would usually continue it.
The marzipan Christmas stollen matches the firm’s seasonal confectionery capabilities, and without evidence of a shortfall management would retain it as part of the holiday range.
Ancient grain bread is still the most experimental variant, yet its survival so far and its reliance on existing baking know-how make continued trial more likely than discontinuation.
